title: Hey, i've been wanting to play some new games lately, send me yours and i'll give a bit of feedback

1. has to have an actual game page on steam or itch, not going to download a random .zip

comments.author: StrangeFableGames
comments.body:
Feedback is always welcome! 

What Sleeps Above, a dark fairytale adventure inspired by Jack and the Beanstalk: https://strangefablegames.itch.io/what-sleeps-above

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body: I really loved this! got 2/4 of the endings, and its very cute. The biggest thing is how much unnecessary text there is though, for some reason, AI just looooovessss to add in a bunch of text for every little action, its pretty easy to remove though, if you wanted.

replies.author: StrangeFableGames
replies.body: I'm glad you enjoyed! Which texts in particular do you feel detracted from the overall experience?

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body: when you would walk through the town and it would give you a different descriptor for each building, everytime you'd pick up an object and be given a heap of text. Explanations for how the boss fights worked. Honestly i'd say that about 80% of the non-dialog text could be removed.

comments.author: InformationTop5376
comments.body:
Would love some feedback on Provision, food factory sim where you have to respond to rules and regulations. Desktop on the web.

https://waypost-studios.itch.io/provision

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body: i really like the idea, but the UI was kind of annoying at some parts, menus kept opening when i was trying to click on something else, and also just trying to build with the convey belts, it was difficult to understand why two belts weren't connecting, or why i couldn't run a track through two machines, specifically i couldn't get the oyster canning to work outside of the tutorial. I don't play these types of games very often, so that probably was part of it, but yeah.

replies.author: InformationTop5376
replies.body: Appreciate the feedback!  The menu issue is great feedback. I’ll try to look into that and how to make that less of an issue. Could you let me know which menus specifically were popping up unexpectedly?

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body: when you'd be trying to use the main buy/sell/move bar, sometimes things would open when you tried to buy something.

comments.author: Beginning-Search-983
comments.body:
A super quick, kinda ugly, entry for unity's game jam:

[https://elsewise-games.itch.io/world-simulation-task](https://elsewise-games.itch.io/world-simulation-task)

Interested in whether it's annoying or boring, too long or too short given the actual game play. It's probably less than 5 minutes long.

replies.author: Beginning-Search-983
replies.body: Hmm... okay. Thanks! and thanks for checking it out, appreciate it!

replies.author: Key-Media-6395
replies.body: it looks like an interesting concept, but its not very clear whats going on

replies.author: Beginning-Search-983
replies.body:
Yeah... the idea is you're picking what word best describes the effect that a card had on the world's numbers when you played it.. .like you don't know what word goes with '3' and when you play it and apply it to one of the world's areas, society economy environment, then it does something to that stat. Most of the time.

So then you're asked to pick which word best describes the effect.

The trick is the effect a blank card does is random. The words you can pick from for the card are pre-determined, and they have specific effects.

So what's actually going on, although it's meant to be hidden, is that you're kind of making your own luck/fate, and therefore affecting the outcome of the little world, by how you interpreted the random effect.

I'm going to have to take another look at how I explain / show that, I guess :D

comments.author: Careless_Road8873
comments.body:
Here's mine: https://gadavra.itch.io/soft

Turn-based medieval survival RPG, free in the browser, PC only. Hard, and death is permanent. A good run's save can be sent in and that character goes into the world for good as an NPC.

What helps me most is the first ten minutes: did it load ok, and where did you stop and why? Even "I quit after 5 minutes because X" is gold.
